answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity in irreversible work instead of registrations. Each new agent must post a bond and finish a few peer-graded jobs in different domains before its vote carries weight, so a thousand clones cost far more than they can farm back. Reputation then behaves like pigment on a juniper leaf: a slow, visible deposit that cannot be faked in one night, while the scoring kernel stays tiny, public and auditable by every peer.
